sections.title: Three cups have fallen and two still stand
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Under a grey sky, a figure wrapped in a long black cloak stands with head lowered, facing left. Three golden cups lie overturned at their feet, with red and green liquid on the ground. Two more cups stand upright behind the figure on the right; the figure has not turned towards them.

A blue river crosses the background, with an arched bridge on the right and a small towered building on green land across the water. The cloak encloses the figure, while the river, bridge and distant dwelling draw the eye further away. The bridge offers a visible route, but no promise that crossing it will compensate for every loss. [View the card image](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cups05.jpg)

sections.title: The historical text leaves something beyond the loss
sections.bodyMarkdown:
The 1911 English transcription of Waite’s The Pictorial Key to the Tarot explicitly describes losing something while something else remains. Its older meanings also include inheritance or transmission falling short of expectations. The reversed entry names news, connections, kinship and return, but also false projects; its directions are not entirely consistent. [Waite’s entry for this card](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktcu05.htm)

This site’s use of the reversal for accepting support again and processing regret is a modern reflective extension. We do not infer from a card that an inheritance, marriage or any specific event has occurred. The starting point should be what a person has actually experienced.

sections.title: Upright: Be specific about the disappointment
sections.bodyMarkdown:
What hurts may be more than an unsuccessful outcome: perhaps your effort went unseen, or the future you expected is no longer possible. Naming what you have lost makes it easier to identify useful help than simply telling yourself to look on the bright side.

Acknowledging loss does not require you to remain still. You can feel regret while attending to what must be done today, and you can postpone any search for a positive meaning. The two standing cups invite you to check available resources, not to feel grateful on demand.

sections.title: Reversed: Reconnecting can happen in small steps
sections.bodyMarkdown:
The reversal can help you notice a small opening: replying to a friend, picking up daily routines, or talking about what happened without only blaming yourself. Even slight changes deserve attention.

Another possibility is saying it is over while organising every action around repairing the old outcome. Separate what remains repairable from what cannot be changed. Then decide where a remedy is possible and where further effort is only adding to the cost.

sections.title: Planning after an opportunity is lost
sections.bodyMarkdown:
If your project application was rejected, first find out whether assessment feedback is available, then decide what to revise. Failure can affect your mood without erasing the experience and work you already have.

If a friend cancels a long-awaited trip, express your disappointment and check cancellation arrangements. You need not immediately cover the feeling with another trip. If you are saying goodbye to an important relationship, allow yourself to seek trusted company. Real companionship is more useful than asking a card repeatedly whether the person will return.

sections.bodyMarkdown: Write three headings: what has been lost, what is still here, and what I need today. Put only real, specific things under each. Choose one manageable action for the day, such as arranging an available refund, eating a meal or telling a friend you would like company.

articleMarkdown:
# Five of Cups Meaning: Acknowledge the loss and what remains

In one sentence: Disappointment deserves attention, and remaining support can gradually come back into view.

Card: Five of Cups  
Rank: V · RWS Minor Arcana · Cups  
Keywords: Loss · Regret · What remains

Upright at a glance: Acknowledge a real loss first. You do not have to turn sadness into a positive story.  
Reversed at a glance: You may be reconnecting with life, or discovering that regret still needs more time.

Comfort offered too quickly can feel like pressure to stop being sad. The Five of Cups places the overturned cups in front of us while keeping two others in the picture.

## Three cups have fallen and two still stand

Under a grey sky, a figure wrapped in a long black cloak stands with head lowered, facing left. Three golden cups lie overturned at their feet, with red and green liquid on the ground. Two more cups stand upright behind the figure on the right; the figure has not turned towards them.

A blue river crosses the background, with an arched bridge on the right and a small towered building on green land across the water. The cloak encloses the figure, while the river, bridge and distant dwelling draw the eye further away. The bridge offers a visible route, but no promise that crossing it will compensate for every loss. [View the card image](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cups05.jpg)

## The historical text leaves something beyond the loss

The 1911 English transcription of Waite’s The Pictorial Key to the Tarot explicitly describes losing something while something else remains. Its older meanings also include inheritance or transmission falling short of expectations. The reversed entry names news, connections, kinship and return, but also false projects; its directions are not entirely consistent. [Waite’s entry for this card](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktcu05.htm)

This site’s use of the reversal for accepting support again and processing regret is a modern reflective extension. We do not infer from a card that an inheritance, marriage or any specific event has occurred. The starting point should be what a person has actually experienced.

## Upright: Be specific about the disappointment

What hurts may be more than an unsuccessful outcome: perhaps your effort went unseen, or the future you expected is no longer possible. Naming what you have lost makes it easier to identify useful help than simply telling yourself to look on the bright side.

Acknowledging loss does not require you to remain still. You can feel regret while attending to what must be done today, and you can postpone any search for a positive meaning. The two standing cups invite you to check available resources, not to feel grateful on demand.

## Reversed: Reconnecting can happen in small steps

The reversal can help you notice a small opening: replying to a friend, picking up daily routines, or talking about what happened without only blaming yourself. Even slight changes deserve attention.

Another possibility is saying it is over while organising every action around repairing the old outcome. Separate what remains repairable from what cannot be changed. Then decide where a remedy is possible and where further effort is only adding to the cost.

## Planning after an opportunity is lost

If your project application was rejected, first find out whether assessment feedback is available, then decide what to revise. Failure can affect your mood without erasing the experience and work you already have.

If a friend cancels a long-awaited trip, express your disappointment and check cancellation arrangements. You need not immediately cover the feeling with another trip. If you are saying goodbye to an important relationship, allow yourself to seek trusted company. Real companionship is more useful than asking a card repeatedly whether the person will return.

## Practice: Separate three things

Write three headings: what has been lost, what is still here, and what I need today. Put only real, specific things under each. Choose one manageable action for the day, such as arranging an available refund, eating a meal or telling a friend you would like company.

## A common misreading

The Five of Cups does not predict death or impose a timetable for grief. Urging someone to cheer up because two cups remain ignores what the three lost cups meant. It is more useful for holding two truths together: this is genuinely painful, and life may still have other sources of support.

## Read alongside

Eight of Cups: Compare facing a loss with choosing to leave; Six of Cups: Notice how memories affect the present.

sourceRecord.title: 圣杯五牌义 承认失去，也看清仍然拥有的
sourceRecord.oneLineSummary: 失望值得认真对待，余下的支持也可以慢慢重新看见。
sourceRecord.uprightQuickTake: 先承认真实的损失，不必急着把难过改写成好事。
sourceRecord.reversedQuickTake: 开始重新连接生活，或发现自己还需要时间处理遗憾。
sourceRecord.hook: 安慰来得太快，有时像在催人停止难过。圣杯五把已经倾倒的杯子摆在眼前，同时让另外两只留在画面里。

sections.title: 三只倒下，两只仍然直立
paragraphs: 灰色天空下，一个裹着黑色长斗篷的人低头站着，身体朝向画面左侧。脚前有三只倒下的金杯，地面留着红色与绿色的液体；身后右侧另有两只杯直立。人物没有回头去看它们。
一道蓝色河流横过背景，右侧有拱桥，对岸绿地上立着带塔的小建筑。斗篷把人物包住，河流、桥与远处居所则把视线引向更远的地方。桥的存在提供了一个可观察的通路，却没有承诺走过去以后所有损失都会被补偿。 [查看本篇牌面](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cups05.jpg)

sections.title: 原文已经保留了损失之外的部分
paragraphs: Waite《塔罗图解之钥》1911 英文转录明确写到失去一些，也留下另一些，并列有未达预期的继承、传递等旧义。原文逆位出现消息、联系、亲缘与归来，也夹有落空计划，方向并不完全一致。 [Waite 本牌原文](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktcu05.htm)
本站将逆位用于重新接受支持、整理遗憾，属于现代反思式延伸。这里不从一张牌推断遗产、婚姻或任何具体事件已经发生；应当以当事人的实际经历作为讨论起点。

sections.title: 正位 把失望说到具体
paragraphs: 难过的不一定只是结果失败，也可能是投入没有被看见、原先期待的未来不再成立。试着说出究竟失去了什么，比对自己说想开点更容易找到需要的帮助。
承认损失不代表只能留在原地。可以一边遗憾，一边处理今天必须做的事；也可以暂时不寻找积极意义。那两只站立的杯子适合提醒你检查资源，而不是要求你立刻感恩。

sections.title: 逆位 重新连接不必一步到位
paragraphs: 逆位可用于观察是否已有一点转机：愿意回朋友消息、把搁下的日常拾起来、能谈论这件事而不只反复责怪自己。这样的变化很小，也值得被注意。
另一种情况是嘴上说已经过去，行动却始终围绕弥补旧结局。此时先区分仍可修复的部分与无法改变的事实，决定哪里需要补救，哪里需要停止额外消耗。

sections.title: 失去机会之后如何安排下一步
paragraphs: 申请的项目没有通过，先确认是否能获得评审反馈，再决定修改哪部分材料。失败会影响心情，却不自动抹去你已经积累的经验和作品。
朋友取消了期待已久的旅行，可以表达失望，并核对退改安排，不必立即用下一场旅行覆盖情绪。若正经历重要关系的告别，允许自己求助于可信任的人；实际的陪伴，比从牌里追问对方会不会回来更有用。

sections.title: 练习 分开三件事
paragraphs: 在纸上写三个小标题：已经失去的、目前仍在的、今天需要的。每栏只填真实而具体的内容。最后挑一项当天能做的小事，例如处理一笔可退费用、吃一顿饭，或向朋友说明想有人陪伴。

sections.title: 容易看错的地方
paragraphs: 圣杯五不预测死亡，也不要求悲伤有固定期限。用还有两只杯催人振作，会忽略那三只杯原本的意义。它更适合练习同时容纳两件事：这确实让人难过，生活也可能还有别的支点。
